tldr: An LLM-agent benchmark shows frontier models solve under a third of end-to-end biomedical ML tasks.
summary: The authors introduce BioML-bench, a benchmark of 24 biomedical machine-learning tasks that agents must solve end to end, from data loading to submission. Tasks span protein engineering, single-cell omics, imaging and drug discovery. Four open-source agent scaffolds are evaluated with several frontier models. Agents often produce valid submissions but rarely beat simple baselines. Performance depends more on the scaffold than on the underlying model.
contributions: Introduces a 24-task benchmark for end-to-end biomedical ML agents
Evaluates four agent scaffolds across frontier language models
Releases the harness, task containers and leaderboard
method: Each task ships a dataset, a description and a held-out metric; agents run in containers with a 24 h budget. Submissions are scored against human leaderboards and simple baselines; 3 seeds per agent-model pair.
results: Best agent beat the median human leaderboard entry on 7 of 24 tasks
Valid submission rate ranged from 62% to 91% across scaffolds

limitations.text: Tasks are limited to publicly available datasets

key_terms.definition: The agent framework (tools, loop, memory) wrapped around a language model.
An output file that the grader can score, regardless of quality.
